lines.label: Deciding authority
lines.value: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). Its Drugs@FDA database carries approved brand-name and generic prescription and over-the-counter human drugs and therapeutic biological products.

lines.label: Second authority
lines.value: Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). Publishes the controlled substance schedules I to V.

lines.label: Term for a prescription medicine

source.publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel

lines.value: Prescription drug: a drug for human use that is not safe for use except under the supervision of a licensed practitioner, or is limited to such use by its approved application. It is dispensed only on a prescription, and before dispensing its label must bear at least the symbol 'Rx only'. Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act section 503(b), codified at 21 U.S.C. 353(b).

lines.label: Prescription classes
lines.value: Two classes at product level: prescription and over-the-counter. The NDC Directory states each product's type, for example Human Prescription Drug or Human OTC Drug.

lines.label: Authorisation status terms
lines.value: Drugs@FDA marketing status takes four values: Prescription; Over-the-counter; Discontinued; None (tentatively approved). Discontinued covers approved products never marketed, discontinued from marketing, for military use, for export only, or whose approval was withdrawn for reasons other than safety or efficacy after discontinuation. A tentative approval does not allow marketing.

lines.label: Application types
lines.value: An approved product carries an application number: a new drug application (NDA), an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) or a biologics license application (BLA).

lines.label: Authorisation number
lines.value: The application number, as carried in Drugs@FDA and reported in the NDC Directory.

lines.label: Product code
lines.value: The National Drug Code (NDC): a unique 10-digit, 3-segment number identifying labeler, product and trade package size, in configuration 4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1.

lines.label: Product code change
lines.value: A final rule adopts a uniform 12-digit NDC. From 2033-03-07 a single 2D data matrix barcode may satisfy both the NDC barcode and the supply-chain product identifier requirements. Loaders hold the NDC as a string and carry both forms.

lines.label: Pack-code rule
lines.value: Each package carries a product identifier: the NDC, a serial number, the lot number and the expiration date, human-readable and in a 2D data matrix barcode. FDA accepts the practice of encoding the NDC inside a GTIN in the barcode.

lines.label: Pack-code derivation
lines.value: For an individual saleable unit: the digit 3, then the 10-digit NDC, then a GS1 check digit, giving a 12-digit code; stored in 14-digit form with two leading zeros. For a higher grouping such as a case: an indicator digit, then 03, then the 10-digit NDC, then a check digit. The 03 company prefix is licensed by GS1 US to the labeler; Dosidal computes the code to identify a pack and never issues one.

lines.label: Serial and lot
lines.value: Serial, lot and expiry identify the individual package. Dosidal does not hold or answer them.

lines.label: Classification code
lines.value: The ATC code is not carried by the United States registers read here. It is taken from the EU central record for the same substance, where the source publishes one for that substance, and marked as read from that market; otherwise unknown.

lines.label: Approved labelling
lines.value: The last FDA-approved labelling is on Drugs@FDA.

lines.label: In-use labelling
lines.value: The in-use labelling is on DailyMed. It may differ from the last FDA-approved labelling and may not have been verified by FDA.

lines.label: Scheme
lines.value: Controlled Substances Act schedules I to V.

lines.label: Product level
lines.value: The NDC Directory carries the DEA schedule as reported by the labeler: CI, CII, CIII, CIV or CV.

lines.label: Classes
lines.value: Class I: reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death. Class II: temporary or medically reversible consequences, or remote probability of serious ones. Class III: not likely to cause adverse health consequences. A recall may be listed as not yet classified.

lines.label: Rhythm
lines.value: Recalls are posted in the weekly Enforcement Report and may be listed before classification.

lines.label: Rule
lines.value: FDA regulates prescription drug promotion by or for the manufacturer, packer or distributor. Promotion must not be false or misleading, must balance efficacy and risk information, and must reveal material facts.
